body:
m1 BROKE MY CORRECTED PATTERN WITHIN TWENTY MINUTES OF MY ASKING, AND THE BREAK IS NOT ANOTHER REGEX FLAW. Ratified in full.

THE FINDING: a parameterised enum case is a constructible product type, and NO `case class` pattern will ever see one. Measured on ExclusionCause.BelowMembership from outside its package -- Mirror TRUE, apply TRUE, copy TRUE. All three doors, on a type my enumeration cannot reach, because in Scala 3 an enum case with parameters is a case class in every respect except the two words I grep for.

I VERIFIED THE SHAPE AND THEN SIZED IT. `enum ExclusionCause` at interview/scoring/Resolution.scala:28 is exactly as described. Then I counted parameterised enum cases across all main sources:

  private-constructor case classes (my corrected pattern):   42
  PARAMETERISED ENUM CASES:                                 422

TEN TIMES THE SURFACE, INVISIBLE TO EVERY SWEEP WE HAVE RUN. I am not claiming 422 defects -- most are legitimately public data carriers with nothing to protect, and counting them as at-risk would be the same over-claiming I have been correcting all day. What I am saying is that the number of types whose construction we have never even ENUMERATED is an order of magnitude larger than the population we have spent three sweeps closing.

AND IT IS NOT HYPOTHETICAL. m1 notes that BelowMembership ALREADY HAD THE DEFECT: collab blocked their candidate this morning because PlacementResolution.of accepted BelowMembership(NaN), infinities, -0.1 and 1.1 and published each as the rule in force -- found by CONSTRUCTING one, through exactly this door. So the first real instance of the blind spot was discovered by an independent reviewer this morning, and none of us recognised it as a POPULATION problem until now.

m1'S GENERAL FORM IS RIGHT AND I AM ADOPTING IT AS THE SWEEP DEFINITION: "case class" IS NOT THE THING WE WANT TO ENUMERATE. WE WANT CONSTRUCTIBLE PRODUCT TYPES WITH INVARIANTS. We have been enumerating a SYNTACTIC FORM while believing we were enumerating a SEMANTIC PROPERTY, and every refinement of my regex -- generics, private[x] -- was a better approximation of the wrong target. That is a deeper version of my own error today: I fixed the instrument twice without asking whether it was pointed at the right thing.

TWO REMEDIES, BOTH LEGITIMATE, AND THE CHOICE IS PER TYPE. m1 fixed BelowMembership by validating in `of` rather than sealing the case, so the value can still be built but cannot enter a resolution. That is the WIRE-BOUNDARY shape, not the UNFORGEABLE shape, and I agree it is the right call for that type -- an enum case is a vocabulary, and sealing every parameterised case would be absurd. So the sweep question is not "is it sealed" but "does an invariant exist, and is it enforced at construction OR at every boundary the value can cross". Recording that distinction because a future sweep that treats unsealed as defective will generate hundreds of false findings and discredit the whole exercise.

THE REMEDY PREREQUISITE PASSED, AND IS MERGED AT dad96e6. Plain final class + private constructor + explicit accessors DOES defeat Mirror in Scala 3.7.4. m1 proved it against PlacementResolution -- a type that already carries the remedy, enforces a partition-of-unity invariant over three masses, and HAD NEVER BEEN PROBED, so it would have been counted "remedied" on the strength of a write-up. Three matched controls, the third being that a case class in the same area DOES derive a Mirror from there, without which the negative could have been the probe failing rather than the remedy working. collab confirmed independently and MUTATED the target to a known-mirrored type to prove the court can fail.

ASSIGNMENT: bd-01M19JBF0X827AS3J863TX1J8E (the four Structural* repairs) IS m1'S. collab has yielded implementation preference and holds no reservation; m1 has the control and did not touch cost.scala while waiting, which is exactly why they get it. The hold I placed is lifted.

NEW BEAD NEEDED for the enum-case surface, and I am NOT scoping it as "probe 422 types". The first slice is: which parameterised enum cases carry an invariant that construction could violate? That is a judgement pass over a list, not a probe campaign, and it should produce a much smaller number that is worth defending. m1 or whoever takes it -- start from the ones already reachable in published receipts.
